Latvia is broadly workable with no legal framework for gender recognition — trans people cannot legally change their gender marker, leaving those who have transitioned in a legal limbo. The most documented institutional failure is the European Court of Human Rights' ruling in Hanovs v. Latvia (2024), which found the country failed to prosecute a homophobic hate crime, violating the prohibition of inhuman treatment and the right to private life.

records.name: Turkey
records.summary_text: Turkey presents real, structured danger for trans visitors — institutionalised, presidential-level hostility that has become state policy. Police profile and detain trans women for identity checks (20 detained in Istanbul in July 2025), trans women have historically been frequent targets of torture and ill-treatment by police, and a trans woman attacked with a knife was herself detained (victim-criminalised). Transphobic attacks and Pride-event violence are documented, and foreign visitors must carry original passports at all times — creating outing risk at the frequent transit checkpoints.
